title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20); we report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, audited provider-call interpretation, an explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational safety requires not only syntactic correctness but correct command ordering, workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break), and dynamic runtime properties. Common operational architectures therefore layer deterministic validators and, in higher-assurance paths, sandboxed emulation after generation to expose runtime-only failures. Prior surveys and system reports document these workflows and motivate combined generate→validate→repair designs [1]–[3]. However, large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation—when the same generated candidate is fed to both conditions—are scarce. We preregistered a paired confirmatory design to quantify that marginal contribution under shared_initial_candidate semantics and constrained but operationally meaningful intent→configuration tasks.
sections.related_work: Recent survey and architecture studies document trends and open problems for LLM-enabled NetOps, arguing for validator- and workflow-centred mitigation strategies [1], [2]. Prototype systems and tool reports show mixed empirical gains from emulation: in some regimes static validators catch most faults, while in others emulation surfaces subtle runtime side effects that static rules miss [1], [3]. Work on verifier-guided LLMs and generate→validate→repair pipelines in adjacent domains (program synthesis, compiler optimization) further motivates paired evaluations that separate generation variability from downstream validation effects. Our study situates a preregistered, artifact-grounded paired comparison within this literature to provide an auditable quantitative datapoint about guarded-stage marginal utility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory plan (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Planned Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) with preregistered minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20. Inclusion rules, deterministic reseed policies for parser failures, and contamination controls were frozen before execution.

Task bank and generation semantics. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 family covering three abstract vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest contained initial_state, expected_final_state, required_command_sequence, and workflow policies (make-before-break, must-be-down-for-fields, group activity constraints). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; in the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses). Per the preregistration we enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair a single sampled initial candidate was produced (one provider call) and that identical candidate was evaluated by both conditions. This isolates downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations and any repair-stage calls) as the only permissible source of between-condition discordance.

Validator and guarded harness. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a rule-based validator performing vendor parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks, workflow atomicity checks, protected-interface invariants, group-level constraints, and final-state conformance; it returns a binary detection flag and a validator_trace. Guarded pipeline: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology, executes normalized CLI commands on vendor-abstracted virtual devices, records runtime observations (admin transitions, transient concurrent downtime, MTU/VLAN application effects, reachability consequences), and maps observations to runtime-detection rules.

Provider-call auditing: meaning of audited fields. Execution artifacts include a provider_call_audit object used for run accounting. Important audited counts and their meanings (artifact-grounded): hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 (total model-call events observed), stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 720, repair: 1} (model calls attributed to pipeline stages), and condition_counts = {"shared": 720, "guarded": 1} (a per-stage attribution: the label "shared" marks the initial generation calls that were shared across both downstream conditions; the label "guarded" marks condition-specific model calls performed during guarded-stage repair). Because shared_initial_candidate semantics reuse the same initial generation for both baseline and guarded evaluations, condition_counts does not enumerate episodes per condition but counts model-call events allocated to pipeline stages. In our run these audited fields explain why hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 despite 720 paired episodes: 720 shared initial calls plus a single repair-stage call executed only in the guarded pipeline; no failed hosted model calls were observed.

Analysis plan. Primary inferential procedure: paired-binary analysis (McNemar-style exact test) with paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Primary analysis used complete-pair handling (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs). Secondary per-class/vendor analyses were prespecified and treated as exploratory with multiplicity adjustment.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 720. Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric outputs are reproduced verbatim from analysis/results.json and corroborating artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 and stage_counts {shared_initial_generation: 720, repair: 1}. The single n10 discordant pair therefore corresponds to either (a) a guarded-emulation observation that the validator lacked a rule to encode, or (b) the single recorded repair-stage model invocation. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics guarantee the same initial candidate for both conditions, any discordance must be attributable to downstream guarded-stage activity. The canonical execution bundle contains the raw per-episode record for the unique discordant pair (searchable in execution/raw_results.jsonl using the archived input-results SHA-256) and the repair-stage transcript; those artifacts permit an independent auditor to determine whether the guarded-only detection was emulation-driven or repair-driven.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The negligible aggregate guarded-stage gain (≈0.0014) is best explained by three artifact-grounded factors: (1) validator ceiling effect — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes the workflow and semantic checks exercised by the curated tasks, producing a baseline success rate of 719/720 and leaving little headroom for emulation to add detections; (2) curated inclusion — parser-validated, deterministic task generation produced a low-adversarial, high-coverage task bank; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics and minimal repair activity — only one repair-stage call occurred (stage_counts: repair = 1), localizing the single discordance.

Operational implications. For pipelines that enforce strong parser-level prevalidation and maintain validators with rule coverage aligned to expected intents, automated sandboxed emulation may provide little marginal detection benefit and could be reserved for high-risk changes. Conversely, in noisy, adversarial, or broader multi-vendor regimes, emulation can reveal runtime semantics and side-effects that static validators miss; our archived artifacts identify concrete seed cases and validator-rule patterns useful for constructing such adversarial banks.

Limitations. The result is narrowly scoped to the preregistered task bank, the single validator implementation, the declared/requested model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a near-zero finding for this constrained regime rather than a general claim about guarded stages.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that isolated the downstream marginal contribution of sandboxed emulation relative to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated NetOps artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a vanishing aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call auditing shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair). The artifact-grounded evidence supports a bounded conclusion: when validators are high-coverage and inputs are parser-validated, guarded emulation can have negligible incremental detection value; targeted follow-up should evaluate adversarial, multi-vendor, and higher-fidelity-emulation regimes. The archived execution manifest and analysis artifacts allow independent verification of every reported numeric result.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.
Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
